structure: Verified by WebFetch 2026-09-21: agents/contracts/ holds routes.json, gates.json, state-machine.json, roles.json, personas/, schemas/, plus per-provider conformance-evidence JSONs (codex, reasonix) and a README.md. README cites 25 personas + 18 frameworks as 'complete'; commit messages cite '32 role projections' elsewhere (the overcount the prior verdict propagated). The 7 hand-authored contracts in agents/contracts/ are inventoried as 7 rows in this ledger; the 11 generated provider packages under agents/providers/ are summarised by the single 'agents/providers/*' reject row because they are projections of the contracts (not individually actionable).

decisions.fork_ground: Generation coupling: forking means adopting the generator script + 11 output trees with machine-owned compiled-block markers. The corpus has no compiler pipeline; adopting one would invert the audit model (curated skills become generated projections). provenance.json decisions.scope already rejects vendor-tool skills on staleness/maintenance grounds.

agents/contracts/routes.json.landedIn: writing-plans/SKILL.md 'Not by themselves reasons to plan' section, commit 56b8894
agents/contracts/routes.json.evidence: Full file read at SHA b6516cf52a7891d797621fdd2a8ca0311e1ae0a9. The contract's `nonSelectors` field lists 9 inputs that MUST NOT escalate the route on their own: file-count, repository-size, max-subs, available-agent-count, security-word-alone, refactor-word-alone, research-word-alone, one-failed-implementation, benchmark-label. The round-1 verdict named 4 of these; the other 5 (max-subs, security-word-alone, refactor-word-alone, research-word-alone, benchmark-label) are not corpus duplicates either. The full 9 are the rule, not 4.
agents/contracts/routes.json.note: adopt-rule (partial): the corpus adopts the nonSelectors discipline — what does NOT trigger a plan — but NOT the rest of routes.json (23-input routeFactsSchema, 9-rule precedenceTable, routeAnalyst role, runOwnerDecision role, capabilityRequirements matrix). Those are a complete routing system; adopting any of them requires adopting the system. The nonSelectors list is mechanically separable: it is 9 short labels plus a one-line rule naming them, and it has no dependency on the schema or operator language. Destination resolved to writing-plans (NOT a new route-classification skill): the rule is about what does not justify a plan, which is the inverse of writing-plans' existing Scope Check (what DOES justify one). Adding a new skill for one rule introduces an abstraction with no other call sites.
agents/contracts/routes.json.caveat: Two corollary risks are not yet covered by the autoprompt rule itself but were added to the writing-plans section: (a) the rule must be read alongside, not instead of, writing-plans' existing 'if the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, suggest breaking this into separate plans' — the two are complementary (don't escalate UP just because inputs look big; DO escalate DOWN when the spec actually spans independent subsystems); (b) the rule does NOT apply when one of the listed inputs co-occurs with a real dependency signal (e.g., a large file count plus proven dependency is no longer excluded by this rule and warrants a multi-task plan). The writing-plans prose states both clarifications. If a future audit finds either clarification wrong, the rule should be revisited, not deleted.

agents/contracts/gates.json + state-mach.evidence: directory listing confirmed; contents not yet read in full.
agents/contracts/gates.json + state-mach.note: adopt-rule: 'freeze-before-check + state-machine-driven retry with non-resetting limits'. Structurally similar to verifying-before-completion's Gate Function (IDENTIFY/RUN/READ/VERIFY) but the corpus's Gate Function does not pin retry-budget discipline. The non-resetting-limits property is a real addition: the corpus's verifying-before-completion does not currently say what to do after N failures.
agents/contracts/gates.json + state-mach.caveat: scope of 'failure' is ambiguous — agent failure vs. check failure vs. tool failure. Must be specified before adopting. The combination of gates.json AND state-machine.json suggests these are two related contracts; read both before deciding whether to fold them as one rule or two.

agents/contracts/codex-live-conformance-.evidence: directory listing confirmed; structure is per-provider conformance evidence JSONs, which matches the 'refuse without current provider conformance evidence' rule.
agents/contracts/codex-live-conformance-.note: adopt-rule: 'refuse any required capability without current provider conformance evidence'. harness-bridge comes closest (it pins --permission-mode plan and --fork-session) but the rule is about CAPABILITY discovery, not ARG translation. The autoprompt model pins per-provider live conformance evidence; the corpus currently relies on static capability flags.
agents/contracts/codex-live-conformance-.caveat: harness-bridge already enforces capability evidence by setting stdin:true/false and refusing CLIs that lack stream-json. The new rule is more general — apply to any capability, not just stream-json. Verify the existing capability flags meet the autoprompt bar before adopting the rule.

agents/contracts/personas/ (25 personas.evidence: directory listing confirmed; README cites 25 personas + 18 frameworks; commits cite 32 role projections (overcount).
agents/contracts/personas/ (25 personas.note: reject: the corpus already names personas by skill (reviewing-for-bloat, verifying-before-completion, dispatching-parallel-agents). The autoprompt personas/ tree is provider-coupled and overlaps with skills it would have to displace.

agents/contracts/roles.json.evidence: directory listing confirmed; contents not read.
agents/contracts/roles.json.note: reject: the file is named roles.json (NOT role-policy.json, which the round-1 verdict flagged). The corpus already names roles by skill (reviewing-for-bloat, verifying-before-completion, dispatching-parallel-agents). Adopting roles.json would add a parallel role vocabulary the corpus does not need.

agents/contracts/schemas/.evidence: directory listing confirmed; schema files not read.
agents/contracts/schemas/.note: reject: schemas/ is a packaging-model artifact (JSON Schema files projected into each provider package). The corpus uses Markdown frontmatter and Python type hints; adopting JSON Schema would introduce a second validation surface.

agents/providers/* (11 generated package.evidence: generator script confirms 11 generated packages exist; the 11 packages themselves were not read (they are machine-owned projections of the contracts, not authored artifacts).
agents/providers/* (11 generated package.note: reject: 11 generated provider packages are projections of the 7 contracts. Adopting them would adopt a generation pipeline the corpus does not have.

agents/contracts/README.md (architecture.note: reject: the architecture framing ('provider-neutral source of truth, generator projects into provider packages') is a packaging model the corpus does not use. audacioustux/agents ships curated Markdown + Python CLI.

summary.fork: no (ground: generation coupling, not file count)

next_steps: Read agents/contracts/gates.json AND state-machine.json in full to specify what 'failure' means under non-resetting retry limits.
Read agents/contracts/codex-live-conformance-evidence.json to confirm the conformance-evidence rule generalises beyond stream-json and meets the harness-bridge bar.
If those two resolve to clear adopt-rule destinations, file 2 PRs targeting verifying-before-completion and harness-bridge. Update this ledger with landedIn SHAs.

reviewer_trail.reviewer: puku-cli (self-corrections during drafting; no separate reviewer pass)
key_corrections: Decision A (fork) and Decision B (extract) are orthogonal; blending them weakens both halves.
The 550-file claim was an overcount. Real structure is 7 hand-authored contracts + 11 generated provider packages.

The corpus has a documented audit schema (docs/audits/cursor-plugins/README.md § Reading a row) with disposition/status/note/evidence/landedIn + caveat; ~20% of adopt-rule recommendations historically fail scrutiny. The proposed verdict skipped this entirely.
Generation coupling (adopting a compiler + machine-owned compiled-block markers) is a sharper fork argument than file count or vendor-paths.
AGENTS.md absence is conditional on provenance.json decisions.paths, not a contradiction. The Python CLI fabrication was unfounded.
reviewer_trail.note: The round-1 verdict and its corrections are bundled in commit 64fed6f on lean-autoprompt-audit. There is no separate round-1 artifact in tree; the trail records the corrections as they happened during drafting, not as a separate reviewer pass.
